feature_expressions.name: water_to_binder
feature_expressions.reason: Water-to-binder ratio is the primary predictor of concrete strength; high error association with water (0.2433) and cement (0.1645) suggests this interaction is underrepresented.

feature_expressions.name: sp_to_cement
feature_expressions.reason: Superplasticizer error association is the highest (0.204); its effect is relative to cement content, so this ratio isolates the dosage effect.

recipe.statement: Adding the water-to-binder ratio and the superplasticizer-to-cement ratio captures the dominant physical drivers of concrete strength that the raw features only partially encode, reducing RMSE.

hypothesis.failure_mode: If the ratios are redundant with existing features, RMSE will not improve and may slightly worsen due to added noise.
hypothesis.expected_effect: RMSE reduction of 0.3-1.0 MPa by providing the model with physically meaningful interaction terms that capture non-linear relationships between water, binder, and admixture content.
hypothesis.uncertainty: Moderate; the physical basis is strong, but LightGBM may already approximate these interactions via splits.
hypothesis.stop_condition: If RMSE does not improve by at least 0.1 MPa over the champion, this feature set is rejected.

feature_expressions.name: total_binder_ratio
feature_expressions.expression: (col("cement") + col("blast_furnace_slag") + col("fly_ash")) / maximum(col("cement") + col("blast_furnace_slag") + col("fly_ash") + col("water") + col("fine_aggregate") + col("coarse_aggregate") + col("superplasticizer"), 1)
feature_expressions.reason: Total binder fraction of the mix; high correlation with strength in concrete physics.

recipe.statement: Adding the total binder ratio (cement + slag + fly_ash) / total mix mass captures the overall binder concentration, which is a primary driver of compressive strength not fully represented by the individual ingredient ratios already in the champion.

hypothesis.failure_mode: No gain if the model already implicitly captures this via individual ingredient splits.
hypothesis.expected_effect: Reduce RMSE by providing a direct, normalized measure of binder content which is a stronger predictor than individual components.
hypothesis.uncertainty: Medium; the model might already approximate this, but explicit normalization often helps tree models with varying total masses.
hypothesis.stop_condition: If RMSE does not improve by at least 0.05 over the champion.

feature_expressions.name: axis_ratio
feature_expressions.reason: Aspect ratio derived from axes, potentially more robust than the existing AspectRation feature

recipe.statement: Adding shape compactness ratios (Area/ConvexArea and Area/Perimeter^2) will improve Macro F1 by providing scale-invariant geometric descriptors that help distinguish bean varieties with similar absolute sizes but different shapes.

hypothesis.failure_mode: linear model may not benefit from non-linear shape ratios if the decision boundaries are already well-captured by existing features
hypothesis.expected_effect: 0.005-0.015 improvement in Macro F1 by providing better-conditioned shape descriptors
hypothesis.uncertainty: Medium; the error associations show ConvexArea and Perimeter are correlated with errors, suggesting shape features are important but the linear model may already be using them effectively
hypothesis.stop_condition: If F1 does not improve by at least 0.002, the shape ratios are redundant with existing features

feature_expressions.name: log_area
feature_expressions.reason: Area has high error association (0.1181) and large scale; log transform normalizes distribution for linear model.

feature_expressions.name: log_perimeter
feature_expressions.reason: Perimeter has high error association (0.1073); log transform reduces skew and scale impact.

recipe.statement: Add log-scaled area and perimeter features to reduce scale dominance and improve linear model separation for small classes like BOMBAY and BARBUNYA.

hypothesis.failure_mode: No gain if linear model already captures scale via regularization or if log transform distorts linear separability.
hypothesis.expected_effect: Improve macro F1 by 0.001-0.005 by reducing scale dominance of Area/Perimeter, aiding small class separation.
hypothesis.uncertainty: Medium; linear models are sensitive to feature scale, but regularization may already mitigate this.
hypothesis.stop_condition: If metric does not exceed 0.9410, abandon scale-focused feature engineering for linear family.
